component.name: Notterizmus
component.summary: Outline editor for book chapter notes

description.p: Notterizmus is an outline editor for taking notes on book chapters. It numbers items automatically (Ⅰ, Ⅰ.1, Ⅰ.1.a) and draws tree lines between them, and it copies the result as formatted text that pastes cleanly into TopCoding.

ul.li: Automatic numbering with Unicode Roman numerals and tree connectors
Bullets for notes, pros and cons; bold, italic, tables and Excalidraw drawings
Paste that recognises outline structure and renumbers it
Undo and redo for text and structure, selection scopes and multiple cursors
Find and replace, and a command search that shows each command's key
Spell checking in English and Bulgarian, chosen per chapter
One autosaved file per book chapter, a list of books and chapters, and earlier versions of each chapter to go back to

description.p: Your notes are kept when they can't be saved, and saved when the app is ended rather than closed.

ul.li: Closing the window with a chapter that can't be saved keeps the window open, writes your edits to the app's data folder and asks what to do. It used to close without saving.
A chapter that can't be saved shows a banner with the reason and Retry, and a dot before its title; the app retries by itself.
Your typing is saved when you log out or shut down, when the app is stopped by a signal, and at least every 5 seconds while you type.
Keep Mine no longer overwrites another program's version that Earlier Versions couldn't keep: yours is saved beside it as a conflict copy.
Earlier Versions copies are written in one step, failures are logged to the journal, and the app says once when Earlier Versions can't be written.

description.p: Assessments from the chapter list, scores in TopCoding's colors, and a question list you can resize.

ul.li: Each chapter in the chapter list ends in a button that opens its assessment, or imports a report for that chapter without asking which chapter.
Revealed scores are colored as TopCoding colors them, in the question list too, and the original score by its percentage. A button in the header bar turns the colors off.
The question list of an assessment can be dragged wider or narrower.

description.p: Practice TopCoding chapter assessments, and pastes that replace the selected text.

ul.li: Assessments: import a TopCoding assessment report from its .txt download, graded or not, and practice each question from a blank answer. Reveal shows your original answer, its score, the sample answer and the feedback, and finished attempts can be compared with the sample answer.
Pasting over selected text replaces it, whatever is pasted.
Bullets after a numbered sub-item that belong to the item above it are set apart by spacer lines.

description.p: Bullets at the top level, faster editing of long chapters, and an Earlier Versions that opens at once.

ul.li: A top-level item can be a bullet: type its trigger at the start, use Ctrl+Shift+Space or the item-type menu, or paste bullets there.
Enter, Tab, undo, Ctrl+Space and large pastes stay quick in long chapters and big books.
Earlier Versions opens at once on big chapters.
Menus and the Ctrl+Space popup give their memory back once they close.
Copy for TopCoding gives tables with drawings the same header cells TopCoding makes itself.

description.p: A question before saving over a chapter changed on disk, safer saves and renumbering, ! and ? bullets, and drawing with the GPU on NVIDIA's driver.

ul.li: If another program changes the open chapter's file, the app asks before saving over it: Reload or Keep Mine.
New ! and ? bullets for important and uncertain points.
Drawing uses the GPU with NVIDIA's driver, and drawings stay sharp in wide windows.
Saves reach the disk and keep the file's permissions, nothing typed is lost when another chapter opens, and renumbering puts everything back if it fails.
Many smaller fixes, among them Shift+click selections, toasts with “&” in a title, books whose names start with a dot, long chapter titles and the drawing window's Cancel.

description.p: Drawings pasted from TopCoding, deleting only what is selected, and drawings that use far less memory.

ul.li: A copy of TopCoding's notes that includes a drawing pastes with the drawing, in Chrome and Firefox.
Delete and Ctrl+X remove only the selected items, not the rest of a heading's section.
Closed drawing windows, chapters no longer shown and undo steps give their memory back, and previews are no larger than they are shown.
Quitting no longer crashes after drawing previews were made.

description.p: Ctrl+A and the editor's other shortcuts work on non-Latin keyboard layouts, such as Bulgarian.
Copy for TopCoding takes drawings along in Firefox too, not only in Chrome.

ul.li: Ctrl+D opens Excalidraw inside the app, offline. Done puts the drawing under the item as a picture; a double-click changes it.
Copy above a drawing copies it alone.
Copy for TopCoding takes drawings along in the form TopCoding's editor accepts.

description.p: Mouse selection, pasted tables and sturdier file handling.

ul.li: Dragging the mouse from one item to another selects whole items, scrolling at the window's edge.
A table copied on its own, or with plain text, is pasted after the current item.
A damaged chapter or settings file is reported instead of keeping the app from starting.
Renumbering, reordering and renaming handle chapters that can't be read or written without losing track of files.
Deleting a top-level item turns its bullets into numbered items.

description.p: Fixes for text, find and earlier versions.

ul.li: Thin strokes stay visible: the top bar of "=" no longer fades so that it looks like "-".
Escape closes the find bar from anywhere in it and from the text.
Ctrl+F on a selected word starts at that word, Search Commands keeps the selection for Bold and Italic, and Enter right after typing acts on what was typed.
Earlier Versions keeps a long history: all of the last day, then one copy per hour, per day and per week as they get older, grouped by day.
Indenting or outdenting an item whose text wraps no longer makes the rows below jump.

description.p: Finding things, earlier versions, and a bigger or smaller text.

ul.li: Find (Ctrl+F) and replace (Ctrl+H or Ctrl+R) across the chapter, table cells included, with Match Case and Whole Words. Replace All is one undo step.
Earlier Versions in the menu: a copy of each chapter is kept when you open it and every 10 minutes while you edit. Preview one and restore it; Ctrl+Z takes it back.
Search Commands (Ctrl+Shift+P) finds any command by name, runs it and shows its key.
Text size: Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0, Ctrl with the scroll wheel, or the row at the top of the menu. Only the chapter's text changes.

description.p: Moving around your books, and learning the controls.

ul.li: A chapter list on the left shows every book with its chapters (F9). Ctrl+PgUp and Ctrl+PgDn open the previous or next chapter, and the list's edge can be dragged to resize it.

Chapter Properties (F2) renames a chapter, changes its number or moves it to another book; F2 on a book renames the book. Drag chapters or press Alt+Up and Alt+Down in the list to reorder them; Delete moves one to the Trash, with Undo.
Getting Started (F1) opens a practice chapter that shows each control. About is now only in the menu.
Chapters saved by a newer version open safely: parts this version doesn't know are kept unchanged and shown read-only.
Fixed warnings printed for chapters with tables.

description.p: Typing aids and a scrolling fix.

ul.li: Ctrl+Space shows spelling fixes and completes the word at the cursor from the chapter, the book's other chapters and the dictionary. Changing an item's type moved to Ctrl+Shift+Space.
Number hotkeys 1–9 and 0 in the Alt+Insert, item and Ctrl+Space popups.
The view follows the cursor, so pressing Enter at the bottom of a full window no longer hides it.
